title: Cross-stitch garden robin sampler
subtitle: A decorative border sampler centred on a robin motif
excerpt: A sampler layout centred on a detailed robin with a decorative border of small leaf and berry motifs around the edge. The design is approximately 110 by 130 stitches and finishes at around 20 by 23 cm on 14-count Aida. It suits a picture frame and makes a straightforward seasonal gift piece.
sourceNotes: Original sampler design. The sampler layout (central motif with repeating border) is a well-established format in British cross-stitch tradition, documented from the 17th century onwards.

glossaryTerms.definition: Cross-stitch worked from a chart by counting threads or Aida squares rather than following a printed guide on the fabric. The stitcher counts from a reference point (usually the chart centre) and reproduces the pattern by counting squares across and down.

content.text: throughout. The repeating border is worked once from the chart and repeated identically on each side; the robin sits at the centre. Working the border first and the robin last makes the counting easier.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 920 (rust), 3776 (orange-red), 400 (dark rust), 433 (brown), 3031 (dark brown), 3782 (mocha), ECRU, 310 (black), 3865 (white), 319 (dark green), 320 (medium green), 321 (red), 815 (dark red)

content.text: Mark the centre and find the border start.
Mark the Aida centre. The sampler border begins eight stitches inside the outer edge of the planned stitching area. Count out from the centre to place the first corner of the border.
Stitch all four border sides before starting the robin.

Work the leaf and berry border motif along all four sides. The corner motifs sit at each intersection. Completing the border first locks the edges of the design space so the robin can be counted inward from the frame.
Stitch the robin at the centre.
Work the robin in 920, 3776, 400, 433, 3031, 3782, and ECRU. The red breast uses 3776 as the primary fill. The back-stitch outline uses 3031 for the body and 310 for the beak and eye ring.
Add holly or berry sprigs below the robin if the chart includes them.
Berry clusters use 321 with 815 as the shadow; leaves use 319 and 320.
Wash in cool water and press face-down on a towel. Mount in a 25 × 28 cm frame. The sampler looks equally good on white or cream mount card.
